name: Starter: Maltese
about: Maltese in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Maltese order.

words.għand: at; have (għandi: I have, għandek: you have)
words.ried: want (irrid: I want, trid: you want)
words.mar: go (mort: I went, tmur: you go)
words.żmien: time (kemm għandek żmien?: how old are you?)
words.pastizz: pastizz, a flaky savory pastry (pastizzi: more than one)
words.lil: to; marks a person as what a verb acts on
words.ħin: time (time of day; time to spare)
words.seta': can, be able (nista': I can, tista': you can)
words.sema': hear, listen (nisma': I hear, smajt: I heard)

jekk-joghgbok.about: Literally if it pleases you; jekk jogħġobkom to more than one person.

items.means: A tea and a water, please.
Good morning! Nice to meet you.
Excuse me, where is my key?
Excuse me, how much is it?
I live in a small house.
The bathroom is in the house.
Excuse me, where is the station?
My mother goes to the city.
I'll go to the city tomorrow.
I have a sister and a brother.
My brother works at the airport.
My sister has a little boy.
The key is on the table.
Is there any milk in the fridge?
The kids are playing in the garden.
I want to drink some water.
We ate at the restaurant yesterday.
I'm going to cook pasta tonight.
The ferry is going to leave at ten.
There are a lot of people at the beach.
Do you want to come to the party?

items.text: Il-ġimgħa d-dieħla se nżur lil ommi.
items.means: I'm going to visit my mom next week.
wrong: Il-ġimgħa d-dieħla se żar lil ommi.

concept.line: The present marks who with a letter in front of the verb and, in the plural, -u or -w at its end: nikteb (I write), tikteb (you write), jikteb (he writes), niktbu (we write), naraw (we see).
Maltese often needs no word for is, or uses hu (he) and hi (she), matching the thing described: Il-kafè sħun (the coffee hot), Fejn hi d-dar?

Close family takes an ending (omm → ommi: my mom, ħu → ħija: my brother); other things take tiegħi (of mine) after them: il-karozza tiegħi (the car of mine); of is ta': il-karozza ta' missieri (the car of my-dad).

words.means: għandi = I have; għandek = you have; m'għandix = I do not have
iċ-ċavetta = the key; ċ-ċavetta = the key

concept.line: A yes-or-no question keeps a statement's order (Titkellem bl-Ingliż?

words.means: titkellem = you speak; nitkellem = I speak; jitkellimx = he does not speak
nifhimx = I do not understand; tifhem = you understand

concept.line: Not wraps the verb, with ma before it (which may shorten to m' before a vowel or a silent għ or h) and -x on its end: Ma nafx (not I-know-not), Ma nikolx laħam (not I-eat-not meat), M'għandix ħin (not-at-me-not time).

words.means: f'dar = in a house; id-dar = the house; fid-dar = in the house
toqgħod = you live; she lives; noqgħod = I live
immur = I go; sejjer = going; tmur = she goes

concept.line: A noun is masculine or feminine, often -a for feminine, and its describing words match it, in the plural too: tifel twil (boy tall), tifla twila (girl tall), tfal twal (children tall).
